articles.title: Tesouro diz que governo prepara pacote de medidas para Lula 4, mas nega definição sobre taxação de títulos isentos com IOF  | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretário Daniel Leal afirmou que pacote de medidas econômicas que está sendo gestado deve ser apresentado pelo ministro da Fazenda e pelo presidente da República oportunamente, e não quis antecipar propostas.
articles.summary: Secretário Daniel Leal afirmou que pacote de medidas econômicas que está sendo gestado deve ser apresentado pelo ministro da Fazenda e pelo presidente da República oportunamente, e não quis antecipar propostas.
articles.body:
O secretário do Tesouro Nacional , Daniel Leal, afirmou nesta quinta-feira (29) que a equipe econômica já está trabalhando em um pacote de medidas para a quarta gestão do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), reeleito para o período de 2027 a 2030, envolvendo também ações para tentar reequilibrar as contas públicas.

Ele declarou que o pacote de medidas econômicas que está sendo gestado deve ser apresentado pelo ministro da Fazenda e pelo presidente da República oportunamente, e não quis antecipar propostas.

"A gente está discutindo vários temas, e vamos continuar falando sobre eles e buscando medidas importantes para sustentabilidade fiscal", disse o secretário do Tesouro.

Leal negou, entretanto, que o governo já tenha uma decisão tomada sobre taxar os chamados "títulos isentos", como LCI e LCA, com o Imposto sobre Operações Financeiras (IOF).

"Até hoje, discussão de fato, para endereçar com alguma medida, não. Debater sobre o tema, sempre. Discussões com esferas superiores vem acontecendo, elas sempre acontecem sobre temas recorrentes, sendo mensurados os impactos. Discussão sempre vai ter sobre esse tema e outros. Mas a conotação de que o governo estuda tributar esses instrumentos com IOF, não há uma medida pronta para ser feita", declarou.

Analistas avaliam que os déficits fiscais recorrentes registrados nos últimos anos pressionam os juros e, consequentemente, aumentam o custo da dívida pública.

Para reduzir essa pressão e conter o avanço do endividamento, defendem um ajuste mais forte nas contas do governo.

Entre os fatores que contribuíram para esse resultado, estão o aumento dos gastos do governo e o reconhecimento de dívidas de gestões anteriores, como os precatórios.

Tesouro diz que governo prepara pacote de medidas para Lula 4. — Foto: Jornal Nacional

articles.title: Governo não anunciou bloqueio do Gás do Povo e do Bolsa Família | G1
articles.standfirst: Posts falsos foram publicados após vitória do petista sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno das eleições 2026. Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome informa que programas seguem em funcionamento e sem cortes em benefícios
articles.summary: Posts falsos foram publicados após vitória do petista sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno das eleições 2026. Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Comba
articles.body:
É #FAKE que Bolsa Família e Vale Gás foram bloqueados — Foto: Reprodução

Circulam nas redes sociais posts sugerindo que o governo federal bloqueou os programas Gás do Povo e Bolsa Família. É #FAKE .

As publicações viralizaram após a vitória de Lula ( PT ) sobre Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) no segundo turno das eleições 2026 , neste domingo (25).

Um post publicado no X nesta terça-feira (27) tem a seguinte legenda: "Além do Bolsa Família e do BPC-LOAS [Benefício de Prestação Continuada, da Lei Orgânica da Assistência Social] serem cortados pelo Lula , agora chegou a vez [do] Gás do Povo de ser bloqueado" .

O conteúdo compartilha um vídeo de 2023, agora exibido fora de contexto. A cena tem uma repórter dizendo: " O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva bloqueou os recursos que seriam destinados ao Auxílio Gás – esse pagamento que já vinha acontecendo há bastante tempo. E agora, com esse bloqueio, pelo menos dois milhões devem ficar comprometidos sem o Auxílio Gás no final de ano" .

Na versão do post viral, há na tela um cartaz com o logotipo do programa Gás do Povo e o enunciado: "Será que vai ser o fim do gás do povo?" . Outra caixa de texto diz: "Segundo jornalista, o governo Lula bloqueia o auxílio gás para dezembro" . Por fim, a tela exibe a frase: "demita um petista" .

Embora seja real – e não um conteúdo fabricado por inteligência artificial (IA) –, aquela reportagem não é atual, conforme sugere o post viral. Na verdade, ela foi publicada em 7 de agosto de 2023 no canal do YouTube da TV Arapuã, ex-afiliada da Rede TV na Paraíba, com este título: "Goverrno bloqueia verba para pagamento do Auxilio Gás até o mês de dezembro de 2023" .

Dois dias antes, a Agência Brasil havia publicado em seu site um texto sobre o mesmo assunto, relatando, que relatava: "O Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS) confirmou neste sábado (5) o bloqueio de verbas previamente orçadas para bancar o pagamento do Auxílio Gás, um dos programas sociais do governo. A pasta, contudo, negou a interrupção no pagamento do benefício" .

Leia outro trecho: "O governo foi obrigado a contingenciar recursos em razão do limite estabelecido pelo teto de gastos de 2023, ainda em vigor. [...] No caso do Auxílio Gás, o ministério afirmou que a despesa bloqueada 'só será executada no mês de dezembro', e que até lá a expectativa é que todos os valores sejam liberados" .

O Auxílio Gás era pago a cada dois meses, no valor de um botijão de gás.

Já o Gás do Povo, instituído em 2025, ampliou o Auxílio Gás e repassa vouchers ou créditos específicos, que só deverão ser usados para a retirada do gás, aumentando o controle sobre o uso do benefício.

Já o post sobre o suposto bloqueio do Bolsa Família foi publicado nesta quarta-feira (28) no X, onde passou de 120 mil visualizações em cinco horas. A legenda alega: "Mas já?" . No vídeo, aparecem duas mulheres, falando diretamente à câmera. Uma delas pergunta: "Néia, conta para mim: o quê que aconteceu lá na Bahia, com seus amigos e familiares?". A resposta diz: "Foram sacar o Bolsa Família hoje, está tudo bloqueado". A primeira mulher, então, pergunta: "Mas já?" . E a outra completa: "Vale Gás também".

Nesta terça-feira (27), o Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS) publicou em seu site oficial uma nota dizendo que "são falsas as alegações de cortes no Bolsa Família. "O programa segue em funcionamento, sem suspensão de pagamentos ou redução dos benefícios. Em outubro, houve reajuste de 15,04%, com o valor mínimo por família passando de R$ 600 para R$ 691."

Outro trecho afirma: "Também são falsas as informações sobre cortes no Gás do Povo. O programa continua garantindo a recarga gratuita do botijão de gás de cozinha de 13 quilos às famílias contempladas. O programa tem orçamento assegurado para 2026 e previsão de recursos na proposta orçamentária de 2027, em análise no Congresso Nacional".

O reajuste do Bolsa Família foi anunciado pelo governo Lula em 17 de setembro , a 17 dias do primeiro turno da eleição. O primeiro repasse com valores atualizados ocorreu em 19 de outubro , sete dias antes do segundo turno, que terminou com o presidente reeleito para seu quarto mandato, após vitória sobre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

À época do anúncio do aumento do programa, o governo negou motivação eleitoral e afirmou que a medida recompõe parte da perda do poder de compra causada pela inflação desde o aumento anterior, três anos atrás. De acordo com dados do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), o Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC) acumulado entre março de 2023 e agosto de 2026 foi de 15,04%.

Economistas e especialistas consultados pelo g1 questionaram o momento da alteração e o risco às contas públicas .

No comunicado desta terça, o MDS alertou que a população deve "verificar as informações nos canais oficiais antes de compartilhá-las": "Dúvidas sobre os programas sociais podem ser esclarecidas pelo Disque Social 121. Informações sobre o Bolsa Família também estão disponíveis nos aplicativos Bolsa Família e Caixa Tem e pelo telefone 111, da Caixa" .

articles.title: Acordo Mercosul-UE: exportações brasileiras crescem 21% em 5 meses | G1
articles.standfirst: Exportações beneficiadas por acordo com a União Europeia crescem 21% em cinco meses; mel e abacate são destaques, diz Mdic.
articles.summary: Com o acordo Mercosul-União Europeia, as exportações brasileiras cresceram 21%, impulsionadas por altas recordes nas vendas de mel, abacate e bens industriais.
articles.body:
Exportações beneficiadas por acordo com a União Europeia crescem 21% em cinco meses; mel e abacate são destaques. — Foto: Freepik

As exportações brasileiras de produtos beneficiados pelo acordo entre Mercosul e União Europeia cresceram 21% nos cinco primeiros meses de aplicação provisória do tratado, informou o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC).

O levantamento compara as vendas realizadas entre maio e setembro de 2026 com as do mesmo período do ano passado. O acordo começou a vigorar provisoriamente em 1º de maio.

Entre os produtos que registraram as maiores altas estão:

Outro destaque foram os transformadores elétricos. As exportações do produto para a União Europeia passaram de zero, entre maio e setembro de 2025, para US$ 39 milhões no mesmo período de 2026.

Segundo o Mdic, os resultados abrangem diferentes setores da pauta exportadora brasileira, de produtos agropecuários a bens industriais. O governo atribui o crescimento, entre outros fatores, ao início da redução ou eliminação de tarifas prevista no acordo.

A secretária de Comércio Exterior, Tatiana Prazeres, afirmou que os primeiros resultados mostram a abertura de oportunidades para produtos brasileiros no mercado europeu. Segundo ela, o governo trabalha para divulgar as novas condições comerciais e apoiar empresas interessadas em exportar.

“Há um potencial importante a ser explorado, tanto para ampliar as vendas de quem já exporta quanto para permitir que novas empresas conquistem espaço no comércio internacional”, afirmou.

O ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços, Márcio Elias Rosa, disse que o acordo cria condições para o Brasil agregar valor à produção e ampliar sua participação no comércio mundial.

As negociações entre Mercosul e União Europeia começaram em 1999 e se estenderam por mais de 25 anos. Os instrumentos do acordo foram assinados em janeiro de 2026, e a aplicação provisória das disposições comerciais começou em 1º de maio.

O tratado prevê a redução ou eliminação gradual de tarifas e estabelece regras para ampliar o comércio entre os dois blocos. Para ter acesso às condições previstas, as empresas brasileiras precisam cumprir as exigências estabelecidas para cada produto.

Mercosul e União Europeia reúnem aproximadamente 720 milhões de pessoas e têm um Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) combinado superior a US$ 22 trilhões.

A União Europeia está entre os principais parceiros comerciais do Brasil. O governo avalia que a ampliação do acesso ao mercado europeu pode aumentar as exportações, diversificar os destinos dos produtos brasileiros e abrir espaço para novas empresas no comércio internacional.

articles.title: Órgão do Senado diz que medidas da campanha pioraram contas públicas e exigirão ajuste maior para reequilibrar economia | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento da IFI aponta que apenas o reajuste do Bolsa Família, a perda da arrecadação das Bets e o pacote dos MEIs representam R$ 40 bilhões de desequilíbrio adicional no orçamento de 2027.
articles.summary: Levantamento da IFI aponta que apenas o reajuste do Bolsa Família, a perda da arrecadação das Bets e o pacote dos MEIs representam R$ 40 bilhões de desequilíbrio adicional no orçamento de 2027.
articles.body:
A Instituição Fiscal Independente (IFI), ligada ao Senado Federal , avaliou nesta quinta-feira (29) que as medidas anunciadas pelo governo eleito do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) durante a campanha presidencial agravaram a situação considerada já delicada das contas públicas.

Por meio do Relatório de Acompanhamento Fiscal (RAF) de outubro, o órgão avaliou que, por isso, será necessário um ajuste fiscal maior, do que o necessário anteriormente, para evitar uma piora da situação econômica do país.

“Desequilíbrio fiscal, pressões inflacionárias, juros altos e baixo crescimento. Romper esse nó górdio deve ser a tarefa número um dentre as ações do futuro governo. Sem um ajuste fiscal consistente não haverá retomada relevante dos investimentos estratégicos, crescimento acelerado, criação de empregos de qualidade, incremento da renda e dinheiro para financiar políticas públicas essenciais", avaliaram os diretores da IFI, Marcus Pestana e Alexandre Andrade.

➡️Levantamento da IFI aponta que apenas o reajuste do Bolsa Família , a perda da arrecadação das Bets e o pacote dos MEIs representam R$ 40 bilhões de desequilíbrio adicional no orçamento de 2027.

Além disso, a campanha do presidente Lula propôs, ainda, a extensão do programa Pé de Meia para o ensino superior e a isenção de tarifa de transporte coletivo nos fins de semana (a ser implementada por meio de Proposta de Emenda Constitucional).

O órgão do Senado Federal projeta, para este ano, um déficit nas contas do governo da ordem de 0,5% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB).

Avalia que, com os novos compromissos assumidos, "é possível imaginar" um déficit primário efetivo potencial de 1% do PIB, em 2027.

A IFI também estima ser necessário um superávit primário de 2,1% do PIB para estabilizar a relação dívida pública /PIB

Por conta disso, a IFI estima que a necessidade de um ajuste fiscal equivalente a algo como 3 pontos do PIB.

➡️O órgão lembra das turbulências no mercado financeiro após a eleição de Lula e avalia que o anúncio, "o mais rápido possível, de um plano de voo consistente e crível para os próximos quatro anos e de quem estará à frente do Ministério da Fazenda poderá acalmar os agentes econômicos e investidores, ancorando as expectativas em novo ponto de equilíbrio".

"A IFI tem alertado, nos últimos anos, que é inevitável um verdadeiro ajuste fiscal, se quisermos desencadear um novo ciclo de desenvolvimento vigoroso e sustentado no país. Isso passa por produzir os superávits primários necessários para estancar o crescimento da dívida, criando o ambiente adequado para a queda das taxas de juros; desengessar o orçamento; rever o perfil dos gastos; aumentar a eficiência; e ampliar substancialmente os investimentos estratégicos estruturantes, sobretudo na infraestrutura e na inovação tecnológica", diz o órgão.

articles.title: 14ª Mostra de Teatro de Petrópolis abre seleção de espetáculos | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições começam em 5 de outubro e vão até 25 de novembro; os projetos serão escolhidos para integrar a programação do evento.
articles.summary: Inscrições começam em 5 de outubro e vão até 25 de novembro; os projetos serão escolhidos para integrar a programação do evento.
articles.body:
Começam no próximo dia 5 de outubro as inscrições para a 14ª Mostra de Teatro de Petrópolis. — Foto: Pedro Rocha e Mariana Rocha

As inscrições para a 14ª Mostra de Teatro de Petrópolis começam em 5 de outubro e seguem até 25 de novembro. Os artistas interessados poderão inscrever seus projetos para seleção. Os trabalhos escolhidos serão apresentados no Centro de Cultura Raul de Leoni. A comissão avaliadora selecionará até oito projetos para compor a programação do evento.

Organizada pelo Grupo Teatral Povo do Cafundó , a Mostra é promovida por meio de recursos do Governo Federal, Ministério da Cultura, Governo do Estado do Rio de Janeiro, Secretaria de Estado de Cultura e Economia Criativa do Rio de Janeiro, por meio da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc.

As produções dos trabalhos selecionados serão contatadas individualmente durante o período de avaliação. A programação, com datas e horários das apresentações, será divulgada no site da Mostra, onde também estará disponível o regulamento do evento:

O local tem apresentações programadas para os dias 15 a 24 de janeiro de 2027.

Além dos troféus de participação, a Mostra de Teatro vai investir R$ 12 mil nos trabalhos selecionados pela curadoria. O evento receberá espetáculos voltados aos públicos adulto e infantil. Não há limite de inscrições enviadas por participante, mas apenas um trabalho de cada participante poderá ser escolhido para a programação.

A Mostra busca fortalecer a cena artística local e incentivar a troca de experiências entre os grupos participantes. Além das apresentações, o evento contará com rodas de conversa após cada espetáculo. Os grupos selecionados deverão assistir e participar de todos os debates. Como acontece tradicionalmente, cada grupo receberá um troféu de participação criado exclusivamente para esta edição pela artista petropolitana Flávia Miranda.

As inscrições podem ser feitas por pessoas jurídicas, incluindo microempreendedores individuais (MEIs). Os interessados em participar, precisam enviar a ficha de inscrição, release, ficha técnica completa do espetáculo, currículo do candidato, breve currículo dos integrantes e fotos da montagem, sendo envio de vídeo em plataformas como YouTube e Vimeo opcional.

No caso de espetáculos inéditos, serão aceitas fotos dos ensaios. Os trabalhos selecionados terão as apresentações registradas em vídeo e contarão com tradução em Libras e audiodescrição.

Inscrições para a 14ª Mostra de Teatro de Petrópolis vão até 25 de novembro — Foto: Pedro Rocha e Mariana Rocha

Segundo a atriz e produtora do evento, Simone Gonçalves, do Grupo Teatral Povo do Cafundó, a Mostra registra aumento no interesse do público a cada edição e vem se firmando como um espaço de encontro e troca entre artistas da cidade. Ela também destaca que a primeira edição da Mostra de Teatro de Petrópolis aconteceu em 1983, com a proposta de reunir em um único evento as produções teatrais locais.

“A proposta é promover uma grande celebração da arte, de forma que todos assistam aos espetáculos dos demais colegas. A ideia é prestigiar essa gama de trabalhos que vêm sendo produzidos na cidade”, pontua a produtora Simone Gonçalves.

articles.title: Contas públicas têm déficit de R$ 5,5 bilhões em setembro; dívida soma 82,9% do PIB, maior nível em cinco anos e meio | G1
articles.standfirst: No acumulado do governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), ou seja, em pouco mais de três anos, a dívida já avançou 11,2 pontos percentuais. Equipe econômica acena com pacote de medidas para conter crescimento.
articles.summary: No acumulado do governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), ou seja, em pouco mais de três anos, a dívida já avançou 11,2 pontos percentuais. Equipe econômica acena com pacote de medidas para conter crescimento.
articles.body:
As contas do setor público consolidado apresentaram um déficit primário de R$ 5,5 bilhões em setembro, informou o Banco Central (BC) nesta quinta-feira (29).

🔎 O déficit primário ocorre quando as receitas com tributos e impostos ficam abaixo das despesas do governo. Se o contrário acontece, o resultado é de superávit primário.

🔎 O resultado não leva em conta o pagamento dos juros da dívida pública, e abrange o governo federal, os estados, municípios e as empresas estatais.

Na comparação com setembro do ano passado, houve melhora, uma vez que foi registrado um saldo negativo de R$ 17,5 bilhões naquele mês.

➡️ O endividamento do setor público, por sua vez, ficou estável continuou em 82,9% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) no mês passado — veja mais abaixo nessa reportagem.

Veja abaixo o desempenho das contas em setembro deste ano:

governo federal registrou saldo positivo de R$ 3,5 bilhões;

estados e municípios tiveram saldo deficitário de R$ 5,6 bilhões;

empresas estatais apresentaram déficit de R$ 3,4 bilhões.

Dinheiro, real, economia, salário mínimo, pagamento, PIB, reais, auxílio, notas, dívidas, contas, endividamento — Foto: Natalia Filippin/G1

No acumulado dos nove primeiros meses deste ano, ainda segundo dados oficiais, as contas públicas registraram um déficit primário de R$ 94,3 bilhões — o equivalente a 0,93% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB).

Com isso, houve piora na comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado, quando foi registrado um saldo negativo de R$ 79,2 bilhões (0,84% do PIB).

No caso somente do governo federal, o resultado ficou negativo em R$ 93,6 bilhões na parcial deste ano, informou o BC, contra um déficit de R$ 99,6 bilhões nos nove primeiros meses de 2025.

Para este ano, a meta é de que as contas do governo tenham um saldo negativo de 0,25% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB), cerca de R$ 34,3 bilhões.

De acordo com o arcabouço fiscal, aprovado em 2023, há um intervalo de tolerância de 0,25 ponto percentual em relação à meta central.

Ou seja: a meta será considerada formalmente cumprida se o governo tiver saldo zero, ou se chegar a um superávit de R$ 68,6 bilhões

O texto, no entanto, permite que o governo retire desse cálculo R$ 67,3 bilhões em despesas. E use esses recursos para pagar, por exemplo, precatórios (gastos com sentenças judiciais, defesa e educação).

Quando se incorporam os juros da dívida pública na conta – no conceito conhecido no mercado como resultado nominal, utilizado para comparação internacional –, houve déficit de R$ 113 bilhões nas contas do setor público em setembro.

➡️ No acumulado em 12 meses até setembro, foi registrado um resultado negativo (déficit) de R$ 1,28 trilhão, ou 9,51% do PIB.

🔎 Esse número é acompanhado com atenção pelas agências de classificação de risco para a definição da nota de crédito dos países, indicador levado em consideração por investidores.

O resultado nominal das contas do setor público sofre impacto do resultado mensal das contas, das atuações do BC no câmbio, e dos juros básicos da economia (Selic) fixados pela instituição para conter a inflação. Atualmente, a taxa Selic está em 13,75% ao ano, patamar elevado.

Segundo o BC, as despesas com juros nominais somaram R$ 1,2 trilhão (8,99% do PIB) em doze meses até setembro deste ano.

Em setembro, segundo números do Banco Central, a dívida do setor público consolidado ficou estável em 82,9% do PIB em setembro — o equivalente a R$ 11,11 trilhões.

➡️ Este é o maior nível para a dívida pública desde março de 2021, quando somava 85,1% do PIB, ou seja, é o maior patamar em mais de cinco anos.

➡️ No acumulado do governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), ou seja, em pouco mais de três anos, a dívida já avançou 11,2 pontos percentuais.

🔎 A alta na dívida no governo Lula está relacionada, principalmente, com o aumento de gastos públicos, que gera mais despesas com juros — um ciclo vicioso que se retroalimenta.

➡️ Para o Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI), que utiliza de um conceito internacional — englobando os títulos públicos na carteira do BC —, o endividamento brasileiro foi bem maior em setembro: 95,2% do PIB.

🔎 A proporção com o PIB é considerada por especialistas como o conceito mais apropriado para medir e comparar a dívida das nações. E o formato de cálculo do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) é adotado internacionalmente.

➡️ Acima de 90% do PIB, o patamar da dívida brasileira está bem acima de nações emergentes e de países da América do Sul, ficando maior, também, do que a média das nações da Zona do Euro (segundo dados do FMI).

Para tentar conter o crescimento da dívida, em 2023 o governo aprovou o chamado "arcabouço fiscal", ou seja, novas regras para as contas públicas em substituição ao teto de gastos.

A norma prevê crescimento das despesas abaixo das receitas, e um limite para gastos. Entretanto, despesas excluídas desse limite continuam pressionando para cima o endividamento.

Analistas pedem um corte robusto de gastos para conter a dívida e proporcionar queda do juro básico.

articles.title: Bunge fecha fábrica de amônia  na Argentina | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa atribui decisão a limitações estruturais da unidade e a mudanças nas condições de mercado e no abastecimento de insumos.
articles.summary: Empresa atribui decisão a limitações estruturais da unidade e a mudanças nas condições de mercado e no abastecimento de insumos.
articles.body:
fabrica da bunge na argentina — Foto: Reprodução redes

A multinacional agroindustrial Bunge decidiu encerrar as operações industriais de uma fábrica em Campana, na província de Buenos Aires, na Argentina.

A unidade produzia amônia e tiossulfato de amônio, substâncias utilizadas na fabricação de fertilizantes.

🔍 A amônia é uma matéria-prima utilizada na fabricação de fertilizantes nitrogenados , como a ureia, aplicada em culturas como milho, trigo, cevada e arroz. Já o tiossulfato de amônio é usado na formulação de fertilizantes líquidos que fornecem nitrogênio e enxofre, nutrientes importantes para o desenvolvimento das plantas.

Segundo a empresa, a decisão foi tomada após uma análise de alternativas operacionais e comerciais.

A Bunge também atribui o fechamento a uma combinação de fatores que "comprometem a viabilidade econômica da operação", entre eles limitações de infraestrutura e tecnologia de uma planta com mais de 50 anos e mudanças nas condições de mercado e no abastecimento de insumos.

➡️ A unidade contava com a participação da Associação de Cooperativas Argentinas (ACA), responsável por uma parcela equivalente a 17,5% da produção, segundo informações do jornal argentino La Nación.

A Bunge é uma multinacional do agronegócio que atua desde a compra e o processamento de grãos até a fabricação de alimentos e ingredientes industriais.

🌾 No Brasil, a empresa comercializa produtos como os óleos Soya, as farinhas Rosa Branca e as margarinas e maioneses de marcas como Primor e Delícia.

Também processa soja para produzir farelo usado na alimentação animal e matérias-primas destinadas à indústria de alimentos e de biocombustíveis.

Em nota enviada ao g1, a Bunge afirmou que o encerramento se restringe à fábrica de Campana e não altera suas demais atividades na Argentina. A empresa também disse que continuará investindo em infraestrutura e ativos produtivos ligados ao processamento de matérias-primas agrícolas no país.

A companhia afirmou ainda que pretende conduzir o processo com respeito aos funcionários afetados, oferecendo informações e apoio e cumprindo as obrigações correspondentes.

articles.title: Déficit das estatais federais sobe para R$ 8,5 bilhões até setembro e bate novo recorde | G1
articles.standfirst: Resultado parcial do ano também já supera déficit recorde para um ano fechado. Em 2024, houve déficit de R$ 6,73 bilhões. Resultado ruim das estatais federais tem sido agravado, principalmente, pela situação dos Correios, que passa por grave crise fiscal.
articles.summary: Resultado parcial do ano também já supera déficit recorde para um ano fechado. Em 2024, houve déficit de R$ 6,73 bilhões. Resultado ruim das estatais federais tem sido agravado, principalmente, pela situação dos Correios, que passa por grave crise fiscal.
articles.body:
O Banco Central (BC) informou nesta sexta-feira (31) que as empresas estatais federais registraram um déficit de R$ 8,5 bilhões de janeiro a setembro deste ano.

🔎O termo "déficit" significa que o gasto somado dessas estatais foi maior que a receita que elas conseguiram gerar no ano.

➡️Esse é o pior resultado para o período da série histórica do BC, que tem início em 2002. Até então, o maior rombo para este período havia ocorrido em 2025 (R$ -6,3 bilhões, sem correção pela inflação).

➡️O resultado, na parcial deste ano, também já supera o resultado negativo recorde para um ano fechado, de 2024, quando foi registrado um déficit de R$ 6,73 bilhões.

A série do Banco Central não considera a Petrobras, a Eletrobras e nem as empresas do setor financeiro (bancos públicos).

O BC lembra que a Petrobras e a Eletrobras foram excluídos do cálculo das estatais federais em 2009, mas explica que a série histórica de anos anteriores foi revisada com base na nova metodologia — sendo válida, portanto, de 2002 em diante.

Entram nesse cálculo empresas como Correios , a Emgepron, a Hemobrás, a Casa da Moeda, a Infraero, o Serpro, a Dataprev e a Emgea.

O conceito do Banco Central considera apenas a variação da dívida, conceito amplamente utilizado em análises fiscais internacionais, enquanto o governo se utiliza do conceito conhecido por "acima da linha" (receitas menos despesas, sem contar juros da dívida).

Sede dos Correios em Palmas, Tocantins — Foto: Djavan Barbosa/TV Anhanguera

➡️No projeto da Lei de Diretrizes Orçamentárias de 2027, encaminhado ao Congresso Nacional em abril deste ano, o governo federal admite que as empresas estatais federais, em déficit desde 2023, continuarão no vermelho até 2030.

➡️ Segundo a Instituição Fiscal Independente (IFI), ligada ao Senado Federal, os indicadores financeiros confirmam uma "deterioração perceptível" da saúde financeira de "parte relevante" das empresas estatais federais — o que eleva o risco para o Tesouro Nacional.

"Essa deterioração não é uniforme nem decorre de uma única causa, mas os dados levantados pela IFI permitem identificar padrões que merecem atenção do ponto de vista da gestão fiscal", acrescentou o órgão, por meio do Relatório de Acompanhamento Fiscal de julho.

➡️O resultado ruim das estatais federais tem sido agravado, principalmente, pela situação dos Correios, que passa por grave crise fiscal, com piora do seu resultado financeiro.

Para enfrentar rombo financeiro, o governo autorizou, em maio deste ano, a estatal a vender seguros, títulos de capitalização e a atuar no mercado de telefonia.

A ideia é que a empresa faça convênios com instituições financeiras para ofertar os serviços. De acordo com o Ministério da Gestão, os Correios executam um plano de reequilíbrio financeiro e reestruturação.

articles.title: Why markets rallied: Sensex jumps over 900 points, Nifty gains 1 per cent; 5 key reasons
articles.summary: Indian stock markets rallied sharply on Thursday, with the Sensex rising over 900 points to close at 74,151 and the Nifty gaining more than 1% to settle
articles.body: Indian stock markets rallied sharply on Thursday, with the Sensex rising over 900 points to close at 74,151 and the Nifty gaining more than 1% to settle at 22,936.75. The gains came on the monthly derivatives expiry day, supported by a firmer rupee, a marginal easing in crude oil prices, the US Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged, and strong corporate earnings. Buying also spread to mid-cap and small-cap stocks, signalling improved investor sentiment after a recent period of consolidation.The Nifty crossed its key 20-day exponential moving average (20-DEMA) level of around 22,825 during the session. It extended its gains through the afternoon as buying picked up across sectors. Realty, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and select banking stocks led the advance.Here are five key factors behind Thursday's market rally.Rupee begins the day on a stronger noteThe rupee opened higher against the US dollar, supporting sentiment in domestic equities. A stronger rupee can help ease the cost of imports, particularly crude oil, which India relies heavily on. Currency movements also influence foreign investors' returns and can affect their appetite for Indian stocks.Crude oil prices ease marginallyBrent crude prices eased slightly but remained elevated at around $114-$115 per barrel. The modest decline offered some relief to oil-importing India, where high crude prices can increase import costs, put pressure on the rupee and fuel inflation.However, concerns over possible supply disruptions in West Asia continued to pose a risk. Sustained relief from high energy costs will depend on whether oil prices decline further.US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steadyThe US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4%, easing concerns about an immediate increase in borrowing costs. The decision supported risk appetite, although persistent inflation concerns remain.The outlook for US interest rates matters for Indian markets because it influences global bond yields, the dollar's strength and foreign fund flows into emerging markets such as India.Strong corporate earnings support buyingPositive corporate earnings helped support buying in select stocks, particularly in realty, FMCG and banking. The gains reflected investor interest in companies with resilient business performance.Analysts, however, said the recovery needs sustained buying across sectors to establish a more durable upward trend.Mid-cap and small-cap stocks join the rallyThe rally extended beyond the benchmark indices, with mid-cap and small-cap stocks also recording solid gains. The broader participation suggested that buying interest had improved following a brief phase of consolidation.Ajit Mishra, senior vice-president of research at Religare Broking, said the recovery reflected improved risk appetite and renewed buying interest."Markets staged a strong rebound on Thursday, gaining over 1% amid favourable cues and improved investor sentiment. After opening on a flat note, the Nifty crossed the key hurdle around 20 DEMA and gradually moved higher to settle at 22,936.75. The Sensex advanced over 900 points to close at 74,151 on the expiry day, reflecting improved risk appetite and renewed buying interest," Mishra said.He added that the breadth of the rally was encouraging, but further gains would require sustained buying across sectors."On the sectoral front, buying was visible across several pockets, with realty, FMCG and select banking stocks leading the recovery. The broad-based advance indicates an improvement in market participation following the recent correction. However, sustained buying across sectors will be essential to establish a more durable recovery."Among the key macro factors, the US Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.75%–4%, while its commentary highlighted persistent inflation concerns. Global bond yields, dollar movements and expectations surrounding the future interest-rate trajectory will therefore remain in focus. Meanwhile, Brent crude eased modestly but continued to trade at elevated levels of around $114–115 per barrel amid persistent concerns over potential supply disruptions in West Asia," Mishra added.What lies ahead for the markets?Technical indicators suggest the Nifty could move towards 23,100-23,300 if buying momentum continues. The 22,500-22,700 range is expected to provide near-term support, while the 22,200-22,400 band remains an important downside level.Mishra cautioned that elevated crude oil prices and global uncertainty could limit the recovery."The recovery was supported by broad-based buying, although elevated crude oil prices and global uncertainty continued to warrant caution. Technically, the Nifty’s move above the 20-DEMA zone around 22,825 offers near-term relief and improves the prospects of an advance towards the 23,100–23,300 zone. However, sustained follow-through buying will be necessary to confirm a meaningful improvement in the market structure. The 22,500–22,700 zone is likely to act as immediate support, while the broader 22,200–22,400 band remains an important downside reference. Traders should use the rebound selectively, avoid aggressive leverage and maintain disciplined risk management. Investors may consider staggered accumulation in fundamentally strong companies at reasonable valuations, while closely monitoring crude oil prices, foreign fund flows and global bond yields," Mishra concluded.You use AI every day. articles.title: IndiGo Q2 loss falls 27% to Rs 1,879 crore; no option but to increase fares, says CEO
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prepare to shell out even more for flying this winter.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prepare to shell out even more for flying this winter. The CEO of India’s largest airline IndiGo Thursday said there’s no “no choice left but to look to increase fares” as it faces a “very significant” rise in its fuel bill. The stark warning came as IndiGo Thursday reported a loss of Rs 1879.1 crore this Q2, 27% lower from the loss of Rs 2,582.1 crore in same period last year as total income rose 24% to Rs 24,311.9 crore.The loss was due to “exceptionally high fuel costs and rupee depreciation.” The airline’s fuel cost rose to Rs 9,966.8 crore this Q2 — up 67.2% from Rs 5,961.8 crore in same period last fiscal — despite capacity getting reduced by 1% to 40.8 billion available seat km (ASKM, a standard aviation metric that measures an airline's total passenger-carrying capacity.)With escalated operating costs leading to higher airfares, the airline saw its passenger ticket revenue rise 29.3% to Rs 20,652.2 crore despite number of flyers falling 4.7% to 2.7 crore and load factor (aircraft occupancy) falling 2.2 points to 80.3% this July-Sept quarter.“We are looking at a period of elevated fuel cost for sometime. We will continue to look at every measure that can be taken internally to offset the very significant increase in our prices,” IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh said as the airline reported a loss for the third consecutive quarter. It does not expect an immediate relief from elevated fuel costs.The budget airline’s scrip closed 0.2% up on BSE Thursday at Rs 4,680 when the broader market was up 1.2%.“The seasonally soft Sept quarter saw exceptionally elevated fuel costs and continued geopolitical turmoil. We responded with prudent capacity reduction and yield management, supporting strong revenue performance but only partially offsetting the higher costs. Despite these actions, the quarter resulted in a net loss of around Rs 1,900 crore. We remain focused on managing the near-term challenges while continuing to invest for the future. India’s long-term aviation opportunity remains compelling, and our priorities remain clear: safe and reliable operations, rigorous cost discipline, and disciplined growth that creates sustainable value,” Walsh added.As on Sept 30, 2026, IndiGo had a total cash balance of Rs 52,685.4 crore comprising Rs 39,929 crore of free cash and Rs 12,756.4 million of restricted cash. The capitalised operating lease liability was Rs 55,159.2 crore. The total debt (including capitalised operating lease liability) was Rs 87,303.1 crore. This Sept end, IndiGo had a fleet of 442 aircraft and it operated a peak of 2,020 daily flights during the quarter including non-scheduled flights.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Bengaluru: Spacetech company Pixxel has set up a US subsidiary to expand its business with American govt agencies, including those in defence and intelligence.The unit, Pixxel Federal, will offer Earth observation technology, software and satellite systems to govt customers. Pixxel already has contracts with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO). The new subsidiary will build on those relationships and pursue more federal business, the company said.Pixxel’s satellites use hyperspectral imaging, a technique that helps identify materials based on how they reflect light. The technology can reveal details that conventional images may miss. The company said its applications include detecting camouflage, identifying mineral deposits, monitoring the environment and tracking crop health.“The US government market represents a significant opportunity for Pixxel as we expand our capabilities beyond hyperspectral imaging into advanced sensing technologies, software, and satellite systems,” said founder and CEO Awais Ahmed.Allyson Jenkins, previously Pixxel’s vice president for the public sector, has been appointed CEO of the subsidiary. She has 18 years of experience in national security and geospatial intelligence, including nine years at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Jenkins joined Pixxel in Jan 2025 and has led its US govt business.The subsidiary’s board includes retired US Army lieutenant general Ray Palumbo, former Northrop Grumman executive Patrick M. Antkowiak and Frank X. Avila, who held leadership roles at the CIA and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.Pixxel Federal also plans to open an office in the Washington, DC, metropolitan area to work more closely with govt customers and partners.The move follows Pixxel’s $100 million Series C funding round, co-led by Temasek and Seraphim, which took its total funding to $195 million. articles.title: US GDP accelerates to 3.4% in the third quarter, giving Trump a messaging boost on eve of midterms
articles.summary: Gross domestic product increased at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter.
articles.body:
The US economy grew at a robust pace in the third quarter, driven by investment, consumer spending, and government spending.

Gross domestic product increased at a 3.4% annualized rat e, according to an initial estimate released Thursday by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis, beating economists' expectations of 3.1% and marking an acceleration from the second quarter's 2.2% growth.

The artificial intelligence build-out was the main engine, with business investment surging 12.7%. Consumer spending grew 3.8%, matching the rate in Q2 and the strongest since the end of 2024. The Conference Board reported this week that consumer confidence is improving, despite sticky inflation and higher gas prices .

Third quarter growth was partly offset by a decrease in exports . Imports, which are subtracted in the calculation of GDP, increased.

The release is the final major report on the economy ahead of next week's midterm elections, as President Trump and Republicans deliver their closing message.

The White House was quick to tout the news. Trump told reporters before heading to a campaign rally, "We had a great morning from the standpoint of GDP." The White House added on X that it was a "'MAJOR BOOST FOR THE ECONOMY.'

Liz Ann Sonders, chief investment strategist at Charles Schwab, added on X that it was "another strong Q for capex. But she pointed out that growth "continues to be somewhat offset by a drag from net exports," noting that the AI build-out "is very import-driven."

Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, wrote on X , "Consumption was still strong. But business investment is turbocharging the U.S. economy."

Molly Moorhead is economics editor at Yahoo Finance.

articles.summary: Virat Kohli’s Agilitas stake rises to 6.4% after NCLT-approved One8 merger, as the sportswear group targets Rs 2,000–3,000 crore growth and global expansion.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Indian cricketer Virat Kohli’s stake in sportswear company Agilitas Sports has increased to 6.4% from 1.8% following the National Company Law Tribunal’s (NCLT) approval of the merger of his sportswear brand One8 with Agilitas.Kohli invested Rs 40 crore in Agilitas last year. Under the merger, One8 Sports has been integrated into Agilitas as a wholly owned subsidiary, with Kohli’s shareholding moving to the parent company. The integration is aimed at fast-tracking Agilitas’ ambition of building a high-performance sportswear label from India.Kohli will continue as co-founder of One8 and remain involved in building the brand, which plans to expand into international markets, including the US, UK, Canada and Australia.The merger gives One8 access to Agilitas’ capabilities in product development, design, research and development, manufacturing and retail. The integration is expected to help the brand enter new sporting categories and markets.Agilitas Sports, co-founded by former Puma India managing director Abhishek Ganguly, told TOI that One8 would be able to leverage the group’s product development and retail capabilities.“The synergies are significant. One8 wants to become a global sportswear brand from India, and that ambition is very strong. One8 will now have full access to Agilitas’ manufacturing, design, product development and R&D capabilities, as well as its brand-building and retail capabilities. We will soon open exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) under the One8 brand,” Ganguly said.Agilitas aims to build One8 into a Rs 2,000-3,000 crore business over the next four to six years. It also plans to enter more international markets, either directly or through distribution partners.“The opportunity to realise a dream of mine in terms of building a sports brand while I was still playing was something I always wanted. I’ve been involved in literally everything from day one, from technology and materials to designing. This is a vision that I feel very strongly about. The aspiration is for the brand to outlast all of us, become a part of people’s lifestyle and ultimately stand on its own,” Kohli said.Agilitas’ portfolio includes One8 and Lotto, along with Mochiko Shoes, its sports footwear manufacturing business, and Sports Yard, its multi-brand retail format.Mochiko manufactures products for brands including Adidas, Puma, New Balance, Skechers, Reebok, Asics, Crocs, Decathlon, Clarks and US Polo. Ganguly said the company’s recent brand launches were gaining traction, with Lotto already generating over Rs 100 crore in its first year in India.Agilitas plans to open 10 Sports Yard stores over the next six months and will soon launch a third brand, Ganguly said. The company also plans to raise equity capital through a private round in the coming months to fund expansion across retail, manufacturing and brand-building.Global examples include China’s Anta, valued at around $28 billion, and Hoka, which has grown significantly over the past decade. Dick’s Sporting Goods, JD Sports and Sports Direct have also expanded, with Dick’s acquiring Foot Locker.“We want Agilitas to become a major global company built out of India. Our ambition goes beyond the domestic market. India should not just import and buy foreign brands; we should build strong homegrown brands and take them to markets around the world. It is an audacious ambition, but our goal is to build a significant global sportswear company from India,” Ganguly said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Cognizant lowers FY26 growth outlook to 4% to 4.4% in constant currency
articles.summary: Cognizant cuts FY26 constant-currency growth outlook to 4%-4.4%, guides 2026 revenue at $22-$22.1B; shares fall on macro uncertainty.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Cognizant shares fell 4.5% in early Nasdaq trade after the IT firm lowered its revenue growth outlook for the second consecutive quarter, expecting 2026 growth to be at the lower end of its original 4-6.5% guidance range. Macroeconomic uncertainty, inflation, policy changes and supply-chain disruptions are delaying client decisions in some sectors.The company expects revenue of $22 billion to $22.1 billion in 2026, representing year-on-year growth of 4.5-4.9%, or 4-4.4% in constant currency. The outlook includes about 150 basis points of contribution from acquisitions.“The change in the outlook reflects two sectors where macroeconomic factors, policy uncertainty, oil prices and supply-chain disruptions are causing decision delays and uncertainty among customers. Momentum in these sectors has been lower than we anticipated in July,” CEO Ravi Kumar S said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call on Thursday.Cognizant guided for revenue growth of 3-4.5% in the March quarter, indicating a slowdown from the Sept quarter. It also revised its expected spending on the Project Leap programme to $180 million-$250 million, citing the redeployment and retraining of more employees than initially planned.In the Sept quarter, revenue rose 4.6% year-on-year to $5.6 billion, or 4.8% in constant currency. Acquisitions, mainly Astreya and 3Cloud, contributed about 210 basis points to growth, while third-party product sales added around 190 basis points.Growth was uneven across business segments. Financial services grew 12.3% in constant currency, marking its third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Health sciences revenue declined 1.1%, while products and resources fell 0.9%. North America grew 5.7%, compared with 1.4% in Europe.Kumar said healthcare spending was affected by regulatory uncertainty around Medicaid and Medicare funding and enrolments. “That uncertainty is affecting enrolment levels and customer spending. As the funding environment becomes clearer, we expect the sector to stabilise. Funding cycles could support a recovery in 2027.”Retail and consumer goods customers remained cautious amid concerns over interest rates, affordability and tariffs.Kumar said AI remained a growth opportunity, with the focus gradually shifting from productivity improvements in existing work to developing new products and services. However, discretionary spending had not picked up as quickly as expected.“As the macroeconomic environment improves, we expect new AI-led opportunities to outpace the productivity-related revenue deflation,” he said.CFO Jatin Dalal said about 50% of Cognizant’s code was now assisted by machines. Revenue per employee rose 3%, while profit per employee increased 5%, reflecting the contribution of digital labour.The bookings mix is also changing, with new expansion bookings rising to 60% of the total from 48%. Trailing 12-month bookings grew 4%, while large-deal bookings rose 9%. The higher share of new business could help bookings translate into revenue faster than renewals, Kumar said.Cognizant added 3,200 employees sequentially, taking its workforce to 3.6 lakh, up about 10,000 year-on-year. Voluntary attrition stood at 12.6%.Dalal said the company had around 32,000 employees in the US, the vast majority of whom were local hires, and planned to recruit close to 1,000 employees through US campus hiring this year. He said immigration changes were not expected to affect its US talent strategy.On the proposed India listing, Dalal said the company was awaiting changes to the regulatory framework and would decide once the final rules were available, which he expected in the coming weeks to a couple of months.You use AI every day. The Department of Education is preparing to restart involuntary debt collections against student loan borrowers in default, according to recent media reports.

That means the government could soon start seizing funds from student borrowers with defaulted loans.

"One of the first avenues of recourse to reimburse the federal government is people getting their tax returns taken away and then credited towards the payment of the debt," said Jack Wallace, student loan expert and director at Yrefy. "Then the Treasury has the ability to garnish wages up to 15% … to satisfy repayment of the debt."

If collections restart, the two methods are known as the Treasury Offset Program, which withholds federal and state tax refunds as well as other federal payments, and Administrative Wage Garnishment, which affects borrowers' disposable income.

The Treasury Department, working alongside the Department of Education, is reportedly looking to hire private debt collectors to restart these collections. In response to a request for comment, the Department of Education told Yahoo Finance, "Involuntary collections remain paused."

Collections on defaulted loans have been paused since the start of the pandemic in March 2020. Earlier this year, the Education Department delayed the resumption of involuntary collections to give borrowers time to resolve their defaulted loans ahead of this year's student loan changes .

Now, more than 9.3 million borrowers in default may face involuntary withholding of their income or federal payments. "It's not a grant, it's not a scholarship — it was a federal student loan," Wallace said. "Loans you have to repay, and now it's time to pay the piper."

But there are still some actions borrowers can take to avoid collections.

How borrowers can avoid wage garnishment

For borrowers who have entered default on their student loans, taking action to get out of defaulted status can help avoid debt collection consequences like wage garnishment.

"The most important thing is people need to be proactive," Wallace said, including contacting your loan servicer and exploring your options on the Federal Student Aid website. He also referred borrowers to the recently launched Defaulted Loans Support Center from the Education Department and Treasury, which has resources for defaulted borrowers.

Here's a look at options for defaulted borrowers:

Ahead of any changes to the ongoing pause, the best thing defaulted borrowers can do is get out of default before collections begin. These are the primary options available today:

Loan rehabilitation is an option for getting out of default that can also remove the record of default from a borrower's credit history.

For Direct Loans, rehabilitation requires a written agreement to make nine on-time monthly payments. Borrowers must then make all nine payments within 10 consecutive months. The loan servicer determines the exact required payment amount based on the borrower's discretionary income. After those payments, your loan will no longer be in default, and you'll no longer be at risk of collections.

Consolidating a defaulted loan into a Direct Consolidation Loan is another option. To consolidate a loan after default, borrowers must agree to repay the new consolidation loan under an income-driven repayment plan.

As an alternative, borrowers can make three consecutive, on-time monthly payments toward the defaulted loan before consolidating. That payment amount is set by the loan servicer. Under this option, borrowers can choose any repayment plan for their new Direct Consolidation Loan after consolidating.

The final option for getting federal student loans out of default is paying them in full. This may not be possible for many borrowers in default, but a lump sum payment can help get loans out of default and avoid involuntary collections.

Involuntary collections, for now, are still paused. There are currently no wage garnishment or Treasury offset actions being taken against borrowers.

However, the Department of Education still offers information for avoiding garnishment and offset. Here's a look at some options for borrowers:

Before involuntary collections begin, borrowers in default will receive notice before their wages are garnished (30 days in advance) or that their federal benefits will be offset (65 days).

After receiving that notice, borrowers may have the option to set up a payment agreement with their loan servicer. The loans will stay in default, but you can establish a repayment agreement and begin paying before the date on the notice to avoid collections.

In some cases, borrowers may be able to argue a valid objection to avoid collections.

After receiving notice for a Treasury offset of federal benefits, borrowers can submit an objection or request for review by mail within the 65 days listed on the notice. You may object, for example, if "you don't owe the debt, you aren't behind on payments, you're currently in bankruptcy, or you are totally and permanently disabled," according to the Federal Student Aid site.

After receiving notice of wage garnishment, borrowers may request a hearing based on their objection by mail within 30 days of their notice. Objections that may qualify for a hearing and subsequent ruling include those based on the following reasons:

the "existence, amount, or enforceability of the debt"

garnishment that would leave you in "extreme financial hardship"

"you've been employed for less than 12 months after having previously been involuntarily separated from employment" so garnishment cannot be used

Borrowers must submit proof of their objection based on the existence, amount, or enforceability of their debt. The hearing will be arranged by the loan servicer and may be in person (at the borrower's cost to attend), by phone, or based on the documents submitted.

articles.title: The 2032 blind spot: Many Americans don't know a 22% Social Security cut is looming
articles.summary: More than one in five Americans are unaware that their monthly Social Security checks could be reduced by roughly 20% in six years, according to a new report...
articles.body:
More than one in five Americans have no idea that their monthly Social Security checks could be slashed by roughly 20% in six years.

Social Security's reserves could run out at the end of 2032, according to the 2026 Social Security and Medicare Trustees' annual report. At that point, if no adjustments are made, the entitlement program's Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) Trust Fund will be able to pay out only around 80% of benefits to seniors.

"Many Americans plan around Social Security as a reliable, steady source of income in retirement," said Tim Pitney, the head of lifetime income distribution at TIAA, which surveyed US adults on the state of the entitlement program .

"But when a benefit cut arrives without awareness or warning, workers who have spent years relying on Social Security as the foundation of their retirement will have fewer savings to fall back on, and far less time to rebuild them."

Social Security benefits are funded through payroll taxes, which are then invested in trust funds and paid out in monthly checks to millions of retirees and Americans with disabilities.

The tax only applies to earnings up to a yearly cap. The maximum amount of earnings subject to the Social Security tax in 2027 will jump to $192,300, up from $184,500 this year.

Workers and their employers each pay 6.2% on wages up to that amount. If you're self-employed, you pay the entire 12.4% payroll tax.

Social Security currently provides monthly benefits to around 71 million Americans and provides the majority of income for 43% of seniors, according to AARP.

The depletion of Social Security's trust fund has been decades in the making.

It's "one of the most predictable events in public policy," said Shai Akabas, vice president of economic policy at the Bipartisan Policy Center. "What's different now is that this serious economic shock of a 22% across-the-board benefit cut has started coming into clear focus."

Raising or eliminating the payroll tax cap has been a thorny topic in Washington in the search for a solution.

"Closing the gap would require raising revenue (a higher payroll tax rate or taxable wage cap), reducing benefits (a later retirement age or slower cost-of-living adjustments) or a combination of both," Torsten Sløk, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, recently wrote. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.) There has even been a proposal to have the Social Security administration borrow heavily and invest the leveraged funds in the stock market.

articles.title: ServiceNow, Fortinet Q3 earnings reports lead software stocks lower as outlooks disappoint
articles.summary: Fortinet stock tumbled 25%, while ServiceNow stock also plunged after both companies posted quarterly results that disappointed Wall Street.
articles.body:
What happened: The broader software sector declined on Thursday, led by ServiceNow ( NOW ) stock, which plummeted more than 25% after the company's fourth quarter outlook fell just short of estimates, rekindling fears that AI competition could pressure its software business.

Fortinet ( FTNT ) stock also tumbled as much as 22% after the cybersecurity company released its Q3 results. Peers CrowdStrike ( CRWD ), Okta ( OKTA ), and Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) all declined more than 6%.

What's behind the move: ServiceNow's current remaining performance obligations (CRPO), or revenue it projects in the coming months, are expected to rise 18.5%, versus 19.4% expected by Wall Street.

ServiceNow CFO Gina Mastantuono pushed back on investors' reaction to the metric in light of overall results.

"CRPO, while it's a good metric that talks about what next year's revenue will look like, it's not perfect. It's a nuanced accounting metric that doesn't necessarily capture all of the momentum in the business," she told Yahoo Finance on Thursday.

Wall Street remained mostly optimistic about the stock. Oppenheimer analyst Brian Schwartz argued that the company's adoption numbers show it isn't being disrupted by AI, even if growth isn't speeding up just yet

"In our view, ServiceNow's AI momentum counters a disruption thesis, although it doesn't establish a clear path to organic reacceleration," Schwartz wrote, advising clients to buy the post-earnings dip. The analyst has a Buy rating and a $165 target on the stock.

Meanwhile, Fortinet's third quarter results beat estimates, but its full-year service revenue forecast was lowered to $5.15 billion to $5.17 billion, down from its previous guidance of $5.18 billion to $5.22 billion and below Wall Street estimates of $5.2 billion, according to Bloomberg data.

"Fortinet's cut to service revenue guidance implies lower attach rates from bundled networking and secure access service edge offerings on its firewall platform," Bloomberg Intelligence analysts noted.

Following the results, Wall Street analysts lowered their valuations on the stock, with BofA cutting Fortinet to Neutral and setting a price target of $140 per share.

Mizuho Securities decreased its price target from $160 to $118, while Piper Sandler analysts slashed their target from $175 to $140.

What else you need to know: Cybersecurity stocks have been major beneficiaries of the AI trade in recent weeks as the use of agents skyrockets, raising demand for security and authentication measures.

Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering the US stock market, publicly traded companies, and commodities.

articles.title: Crocs stock soars 25% as HeyDude sales return to growth
articles.summary: Crocs stock soared 25% on Thursday as investors cheered on a return to growth for the footwear company's HeyDude loafer brand and a brighter outlook for 2026...
articles.body:
Crocs ( CROX ) stock soared 25% on Thursday to its highest price in over two years as investors cheered on a return to growth for the footwear company's HeyDude loafer brand and a brighter outlook for 2026 sales.

In the third quarter, HeyDude revenue increased 6.1% over the previous year to $170 million, marking the first sales increase in six quarters for the struggling shoe brand.

Crocs bought HeyDude for $2.5 billion in 2022, its largest acquisition ever. But the brand struggled amid excess inventory and discounting, causing investors to become fed up with lagging sales.

HeyDude makes up roughly 16% of Crocs' total revenue, while the flagship Crocs brand accounts for the remaining 84% of sales.

The return to growth for HeyDude marked "an important milestone" for the company, Crocs CEO Andrew Rees said in an earnings release . The company has spent the past few years trying to reduce bloated inventories and drum up excitement for the brand aimed at younger consumers through collaborations with brands like Buc-ees .

HeyDude marked just one part of a strong quarter for Crocs and is one chapter in the company's broader turnaround story.

Another success story, as my colleague Hamza Shaban pointed out this month, has been Crocs' ability to tame its input costs for oil-derived clogs as energy prices soared.

In the third quarter, overall revenue increased 4.6% year over year to $1.04 billion, beating the Street's expectations for $1 billion in sales, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. Adjusted gross margins also swelled to 60.3%, up from 58.5% a year ago.

Adjusted earnings per share grew 26.4% year over year to $3.69, beating Wall Street's estimates of $3.31 per share.

On the back of the top- and bottom-line beats, Crocs raised its 2026 revenue and earnings per share guidance for the third time this year.

The company now expects revenue to increase 3% year over year, up from its previous guidance of up 1% to 2%. It sees adjusted earnings per share in a range of $14.45 to $14.65, up from $13.70 to $14 previously.

"Results and guide are legitimately solid, and our estimates will move higher," Stifel analysts wrote in a note. "HEYDUDE is stabilizing in real-time … though the magnitude of revenue upside vs. prevailing expectations requires consideration of the new revenue level, and capacity from which to grow."

Crocs stock is up 74% year to date. It's roughly 20% below its all-time high closing price of $180.57, reached in November 2021.

articles.title: Universal Music Subscription Revenue Growth Shows Improvement
articles.summary: Universal Music Group NV reported an increase in subscription revenue in the third quarter, buoyed by price increases and “healthy” subscriber growth, helpin...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Universal Music Group NV reported an increase in subscription revenue in the third quarter, buoyed by price increases and "healthy" subscriber growth, helping the world's largest music label bounce back after two disappointing periods.

Subscription revenue jumped 19% in constant currencies, or 9.5% excluding the firm's recent acquisition of Downtown Music, to €1.42 billion.

Universal has been struggling to convince investors it can continue to increase market share and extract more money per listener, while navigating the threat from artificial intelligence. Its plan, known as Streaming 2.0, involves better monetization of so-called superfans through paid subscription tiers and opportunities for deeper engagement with their favorite artists.

"Our results show the enduring value of backing extraordinary artists, bold ideas, and the teams and technology that help bring their work to the world," Chief Executive Officer Lucian Grainge said in a statement.

The Amsterdam-listed company's share price is down 29% this year and touched a record low in September.

The sagging stock has prompted discussions about whether Universal would be better off as a private company. The label, which owns the rights to some of the world's most famous artists including Taylor Swift and Chappell Roan, has discussed going private with a few prominent Wall Street firms, Bloomberg News reported earlier this week. Apollo Global Management Inc., TPG Inc. and Blackstone Inc. were among the firms with whom management held preliminary conversations, according to people familiar with the matter.

In May, Universal rejected a complex offer from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management, which proposed moving the company's listing to New York from Amsterdam. Ackman estimated that the deal would value Universal Music at about €56 billion through a combination of financial reorganization and a fresh listing venue, roughly double its current market capitalization. Ackman sold his €1.42 billion stake in the company shortly after the rejection.

The music industry has been fighting to stay ahead of the risks posed by artificial intelligence, striking deals with AI firms and taking legal action to protect their valuable catalogs. Streaming platform Spotify reported an increase in paying subscribers in the third quarter, suggesting the broader music industry is weathering the shift caused by AI.

articles.title: These 3 sectors could be in focus next year in Washington — no matter who wins on Tuesday
articles.summary: The 2026 campaign has featured bipartisan calls for action on pharmaceuticals, the housing market, and AI data centers.
articles.body:
The 2026 campaign has featured bipartisan calls for action on pharmaceuticals, the housing market, and AI data centers, a sign that this trio of sectors may be in focus in Washington no matter which party prevails on Tuesday.

The critical comments are especially notable coming from Republicans. Democratic rhetoric about reining in big business is nothing new, but the GOP's focus indicates both an increased willingness within the party to adopt a populist stance and a potential openness to strike deals in the new power-sharing landscape.

And the high likelihood of Democrats winning control of at least one chamber of Congress could also elevate these issues — with or without President Trump's support.

While Democrats are now strongly favored to win a majority in the House in next week's midterms, the Senate is less clear, and a 60-vote threshold there means action would require bipartisan buy-in within any scenario.

That is always a heavy lift in today's increasingly polarized Washington, but the housing issue provided proof of concept this year, after a major piece of legislation passed and became law despite Trump's refusal to sign it .

The coming year is likely to feature "meaningful opportunities and risks for key sectors," Stifel chief Washington policy strategist Brian Gardner wrote in a recent note to clients.

He suggested tech companies and data center operators will face challenging headlines, but "risks are low that Congress would pass heavy-handed legislation ... we expect that it would enact a light-touch framework."

He added that the healthcare sector could be in closer focus, writing "a change in power on Capitol Hill could be seen as a negative for pharmaceuticals as Democrats and the White House might agree to further regulate drug prices."

Calls to 'put the squeeze on Big Pharma'

Pharmaceuticals are a prime example of this dynamic, with a high volume of campaign-trail rhetoric coming from both parties.

GOP Senate hopeful Mike Rogers of Michigan cut an ad saying "the pharmaceutical companies are ripping American families off," while Iowa Republican Ashley Hinson is pledging to "put the squeeze on Big Pharma."

That means — regardless of whether Rogers, Hinson, or their Democratic opponents win next Tuesday — openly critical lawmakers will head to Washington amid prominent areas of bipartisan agreement on regulating drug companies.

One dramatic and notable bill, titled the Break Up Big Medicine Act, would take aim at vertical integration in the healthcare system. It is being pushed by two lawmakers who agree on little else: Republican Josh Hawley and Democrat Elizabeth Warren.

articles.title: Nvidia's relationship with China just got even more complicated as report says Jensen Huang was target of spy plot
articles.summary: Recent media reports have highlighted Nvidia's delicate relationship with China.
articles.body:
Nvidia's ( NVDA ) business is booming, but one sector of the market remains a seemingly impenetrable morass for the world's leading chip designer: China.

For years, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has struggled to gain a foothold in the world's second-largest economy, due in large part to restrictions imposed by the Department of Commerce, which regulates international chip sales. Seeking inroads, Huang has repeatedly urged the White House to loosen those restrictions, which the administration says are necessary for national security and for the US to remain ahead in the AI race.

When Nvidia last reported earnings, forward guidance once again omitted sales projections for China, continually snarled by state politics.

The complicated relationship between Nvidia and China was thrust back into public light on Thursday after the New York Times reported new US intelligence efforts. The US intelligence service, the report says, believes a Chinese national named Alice Huang — who has served as a leader of Nvidia chip customer Megaspeed and who maintains a well-documented relationship with Huang himself — has acted as an intelligence asset and passed information to the governing party in Beijing.

The reporting raises major questions about potential information leakage from Nvidia to China, not only regarding trade secrets but also about Jensen Huang's increasingly deep ties to the White House as he has lobbied for eased restrictions. At a company event in September, Huang took a call from Trump on stage, putting the US leader on speakerphone as Trump dismissed fears around AI's security implications as a "scam."

The race between the US and China to develop and disseminate their own AI technology has, over the past several years, become a paramount concern for the leadership of both governments.

While China has matched or even surpassed the US on the development and distribution of "open weight" AI models, which often come at far cheaper costs than "closed weight" alternatives, the US frontier labs such as Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) have retained the lead in developing the most advanced models.

Powering those advanced models are chips designed by Nvidia, whose leading semiconductors are often regarded as the gold standard for computing performance. While the chips are hugely popular in the US and other global markets, the Commerce Department has, since 2022, blocked Nvidia from selling successive generations of its chips to Chinese buyers as Washington seeks to maintain its edge over Beijing.

articles.title: ADT stock surges to 5-year high after Thrive Holdings agrees to $7.6 billion buyout deal
articles.summary: Home security company ADT agreed on Thursday to be acquired and taken private by Thrive Holdings in an all-cash deal that values the company at $7.6 billion.
articles.body:
Home security company ADT ( ADT ) agreed on Thursday to be acquired and taken private by Thrive Holdings in an all-cash deal that values the company at $7.6 billion.

Thrive Holdings will pay $10 per share in cash for ADT, representing a 45.6% premium over ADT stock's closing price on Oct. 27.

ADT stock soared 34% to around $9.93 per share on the news, putting it on pace for its highest close since August 2021.

Thrive Holdings is a private capital group founded by Josh Kushner and backed by OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), focused on acquiring enterprise businesses for the long term and advancing their artificial intelligence and technological capabilities.

Thrive currently operates 75 businesses across accounting, IT services, and the built environment.

"ADT has spent generations showing up for people when it matters most," Thrive Holdings partner Kareem Zaki said in a press release . "We intend to build on that foundation by strengthening ADT's technology and product capabilities, with the capital and patience to invest over decades. Our ambition is to help ADT's teams better serve customers and offer a seamless service with more actionable information for the professionals responding."

This story is developing. Check back for updates.

articles.title: Alphabet heads for a $500 billion drop in market value, the biggest in its history
articles.summary: Alphabet is on track for its worst day ever, with nearly $500 billion in market value at stake, the second-biggest one-day wipeout for a US-listed stock.
articles.body:
Alphabet ( GOOGL ) is on track for its worst day ever. The stock fell about 13% Thursday after its third quarter results , steeper than any session since it went public in 2004, including its drops in March 2020 and September 2008.

At its low, Alphabet had lost $524 billion in stock market value, the second-biggest one-day loss ever for a US-listed company. Only Nvidia ( NVDA ) has lost more, about $593 billion on Jan. 27, 2025, the day China's DeepSeek rattled AI investors.

Alphabet would need to close at about $274.75, down roughly 15%, to take Nvidia's record, by Yahoo Finance calculations. A close at $282.34 or lower would lock in a full $500 billion loss. It has already blown past the $400 billion SpaceX (SPCX) lost on June 22, the previous No. 2.

In dollars, it's Alphabet's worst day by far. Its previous worst was about $275 billion on July 23. It's also on track for the stock's steepest drop after an earnings report since the company went public, according to Bespoke Investment Group . The previous low was a slide of nearly 10% in July 2008.

The quarter gave both sides plenty to argue over. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to about $31 billion, and the Gemini app passed 1 billion users. But search revenue grew 12% to about $63 billion, short of Wall Street's roughly $65 billion estimate. Free cash flow — the cash left after paying for things like data centers — swung to a loss of about $9 billion as AI spending climbed. The company's stakes in AI labs cost it too.

"The bears will argue this is the first quarter that AI is starting to seriously hurt their search business," Pivotal Research CEO Jeffrey Wlodarczak said in a rundown of why investors hated the quarter .

CFRA's Angelo Zino was more patient, telling Yahoo Finance the pullback "probably represents a buying opportunity."

US-listed stocks have shed $200 billion or more in a single session 18 times this year through Wednesday. That's up from 13 in all of 2025 and none before 2022, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from Bloomberg data. Alphabet alone has lost about $1.4 trillion since its record in May.

Amazon ( AMZN ) reports after Thursday's close, the last of the big three cloud providers to report this week. Faster growth at Amazon Web Services without a hit to cash flow would point to a problem specific to Google's search business. Another quarter of cash burn would put the whole AI spending trade back on the defensive.
